Stone Guildhall

A buildable version of the approved two tower trading hall. Follow the layers from Y=0 upward. The roofed hall has eight interior trading stalls; the right arcade has four more.

Use a north-up map: X increases east (right on the map), Z increases south (down the map), and the entrance faces north at Z=0. The origin is the northwest corner. All left/right labels refer to the map. Choose your floor height as local Y=0; add your world's origin coordinates to these local coordinates. Empty squares mean air.

Inside the building

Interior & trade layout

The central aisle runs X=9–13. Four villager cells sit behind fences on each side. The covered exterior arcade on the right contains four more.

Gold V marks a villager's starting position; villagers can move within their pens. Gold outlines mark job blocks. The brown strip is the clear center aisle.

Access and villager placement
  1. Walk through the front gate at X=9–13, Z=0–5, then through the hall opening at X=10–12, Z=6.
  2. Finish the structure and the Y=3 slab shelves before moving villagers in. Leave the marked front-fence cell and workstation empty in every unused pen.
  3. Set up one pen at a time: place its job block while the pen is empty and its fence gap is open, guide one unemployed adult villager inside, then close the gap. During daytime work hours, confirm the intended profession before setting up the next pen. Keep that job block in place for restocking.
  4. The move-in fence cells are X=8/14 at Z=9,13,17,21 inside, and X=21 at Z=10,14,18,22 in the arcade, all at Y=1. The slab directly above each workstation leaves too little headroom for an adult villager to stand on top of it.
  5. Walk around outside to enter the hollow front towers through their rear openings at X=2 and X=20, Z=5. Ladders reach the upper platforms; the openings at Z=3 connect those platforms to the gatehouse roof deck.
  6. Customers reach the four right arcade stalls from the three block wide path at X=23–25.

This is a Java Edition building and villager setup guide using vanilla blocks available since 1.17. Bedrock workstation and village setup is not covered. Small decorative marks in the concept image are interpreted using the listed blocks. The coordinate maps, placement table and CSV are the authoritative instructions. Mojang's Java workstation notes explain why each villager needs access to its own job block.
